html:
The Guipuzcoan Company of Caracas was a Basque trading company that held a monopoly on trade between Spain and Venezuela from 1728 to 1785. Its main business was cacao.

In the 1700s Venezuela was one of the world's main sources of cacao, grown on coastal estates by enslaved Africans and sold to Mexico and Spain for chocolate. Smugglers, mostly Dutch from Curaçao, took much of it. The crown gave the company the trade in return for fighting smuggling, and it built ports, warehouses and coast guard ships.

The company paid planters low prices and charged high ones, and in 1749 a rising led by Juan Francisco de León forced the government to listen. It was dissolved in 1785. It made Caracas richer and its creoles more resentful of Spain, a step towards independence. The trade belongs to the long story of cacao in Venezuela.
sum: The Guipuzcoan Company of Caracas was a Basque trading company that held a monopoly on trade between Spain and Venezuela from 1728 to 1785. Its main business was cacao.
